opportunities.title: Henry Moore Grants

amount.raw: New Projects and Commissions max £20,000; Acquisitions and Collections max £20,000; Conferences, Lectures and Publications max £5,000; Long-Term Research max £20,000; Research and Travel max £2,500

opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK and international non-profit organisations (established and operating for at least 12 months) for exhibitions, catalogues, commissions, conferences, research, non-commercial publications, acquisitions, conservation, cataloguing and display; individual sculpture historians, academics and conservators can apply to the Research and Travel category. Not for individuals independently developing their own practice.
opportunities.summary: Grants supporting the growth and development of sculpture across historical, modern and contemporary registers, and research that expands the appreciation of sculpture. Categories: New Projects and Commissions, Acquisitions and Collections, Conferences/Lectures/Publications, Long-Term Research, and Research and Travel. Applications considered four times per year via Flexi-Grant.

opportunities.title: Visiting Research Fellowships

amount.raw: Expenses allocation: UK up to £600, Europe up to £700, Rest of world up to £1,000; plus accommodation in Leeds or Hertfordshire

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Artists and researchers (academics, curators working on historic and contemporary sculpture) able to use the Research Library, Archive of Sculptors' Papers and Leeds Sculpture Collections; fellowships at Studios & Gardens are limited to projects related to Henry Moore. Senior Fellowships for established scholars.
opportunities.summary: Fellowships enabling artists and researchers to spend a month using the Henry Moore Institute's research facilities in Leeds or Hertfordshire, including accommodation, travel and subsistence expenses. Types: Visiting Research Fellowships, Artist Research Fellowships, and Senior Fellowships (six weeks). Applications are currently closed for 2026/27; the next round opens in spring 2027.

opportunities.title: Dissertation Prize

amount.raw: BA dissertation £250 cash prize; MA dissertation £250 cash prize; both winners also receive Henry Moore Institute publications to the cover price value of £50

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to BA and MA students of all disciplines whose dissertation was submitted within the past academic year at a UK university, on a topic relating directly to sculpture.
opportunities.summary: Two annual prizes for extended pieces of writing on contemporary, modern or historical sculpture, awarded to the best BA and MA dissertations. Submissions should have a strong focus on primary and secondary sources and original research. The 2026 prize submissions will open in autumn.
